title: Couples Share Musical Taste More than Personality
paragraphs: Many people believe that couples should have similar personalities or values. But according to a new study, romantic partners are actually more likely to share their taste in music.

The study was carried out by researchers at the University of Innsbruck in Austria, led by Julia Vigl and Marcel Zentner, and published in the journal Social Psychological and Personality Science. The research included three separate studies with a total of 309 couples, most of them from Germany and Austria.

The partners in each couple answered questionnaires separately. They rated how much they liked different music genres and named their favorite and least favorite artists. To measure similarity even when partners named different artists, the researchers used online tags that describe music styles. They also asked the couples about their personalities and values.

The researchers then compared real couples with "pseudo-couples," pairs of people who were randomly matched together. This helped them check whether couples' similarities were greater than what would be expected by chance.

The results showed that real couples were much more alike in their music preferences than random pairs. Importantly, their similarity in music was greater than their similarity in personality or values.

The study also looked at whether shared music taste was linked to happier relationships. The effect was small. For example, couples who shared favorite artists reported slightly more tenderness. Interestingly, in one study, sharing the same least favorite artists was linked to a slight increase in love and satisfaction.

Zentner explained that shared musical taste is not what makes or breaks a relationship, but it seems to help a little. The researcher also stressed that the findings do not mean that couples with different musical tastes are incompatible.

The researchers noted that their study only shows a connection. It cannot show whether sharing music improves relationships, whether partners become more alike over time, or whether people with similar tastes simply choose each other. To learn more, the team is now carrying out further research, including a long-term study of new couples.
